articles.title: Antagonistic narcissism is linked to cold feelings toward psychologists
articles.summary: People with antagonistic narcissistic traits often view mental health treatment negatively because they harbor cold feelings toward psychologists and psychiatrists. However, a recent study reveals that self-promotional narcissistic traits might actually encourage more favorable views of therapy.

articles.title: RBS-Attention: Radius-Bounded Sparse Prefill for Long-Context Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.20971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-context large language model inference is increasingly limited by prefill, where dense self-attention processes the entire prompt before generation begins. Sparse block selection can reduce this cost, but a block centroid may hide a highly relevant token among many irrelevant ones. We call this failure mode mean dilution and propose RBS-Attention, a training-free sparse-prefill method with two complementary selection branches. articles.summary: arXiv:2609.20974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Mixture-of-Experts language models, the router typically selects and weights experts based on the token's hidden state, utilizing limited contextual information. We propose Attention-Aware Routing (AAR), which augments the router with temporal and spectral features extracted from a sliding window of attention weights that represent a summary of the model's contextual state, disentangled from the hidden state. articles.title: Brain scans reveal how artificial sweeteners affect our reward circuits differently than sugar
articles.summary: A new study reveals that while zero-calorie sweeteners generally affect the body like water, they trigger distinct activity in the brain’s reward centers compared to real sugar. Interestingly, some even delay stomach emptying without spiking blood sugar.

articles.title: Mental health conditions are lasting longer today than they did a decade ago
articles.summary: Recent research indicates a troubling trend: common mental health conditions like anxiety and depression are lasting substantially longer today than they did a decade ago. The findings highlight growing challenges for long-term recovery and psychiatric care.

articles.title: Advanced math for whom? Study shows wealth rivals academic readiness in high school tracking
articles.summary: A comprehensive analysis of American high schools reveals that while students are largely sorted into math and science classes based on academic readiness, the social and economic status of a community also dictates access to advanced coursework.

articles.title: Binding-Motivated Contextuality: A Cross-Domain Cyclic Test in Perception and Judgment
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.23977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perceptual binding and the contextuality of judgment are studied apart, in psychophysics and decision research. We argue they share one obstruction: a nonzero class in $H^1$ of a presheaf with no global section -- though only contextuality is tested, since binding's obstruction vanishes. We build on sheaf formulations of predictive coding (Seely 2025) and contextuality (Abramsky & Brandenburger 2011): a cyclic set of pairwise judgments admits a global (noncontextual) explanation exactly when the cyclic (Suppes-Zanotti / n-cycle) inequalities hold

articles.title: Stem cells reverse stroke damage and restore movement in mice
articles.summary: Stem cell transplants helped regenerate stroke-damaged brain tissue in mice, producing new neurons and restoring lost motor function. The treatment also improved blood vessels, inflammation, and the blood-brain barrier, raising hopes that a similar approach could eventually help repair the human brain after stroke.

articles.title: Scientists create a needle-thin brain implant that can do three jobs at once
articles.summary: A new needle-thin brain implant can record neural activity, deliver drugs, and stimulate multiple brain regions using a single flexible fiber. Successful tests in mice suggest it could give scientists a more precise, less invasive way to study the brain and may eventually help treat neurological disorders such as epilepsy.

articles.title: Brain scans reveal a possible cause of long COVID fatigue and brain fog
articles.summary: Researchers have found evidence that long COVID may damage dopamine releasing neurons in the brain, potentially explaining persistent fatigue, low motivation, slowed movement, and memory difficulties. The discovery could lead to new treatments that target the brain's dopamine system.

articles.title: Psychologists pinpoint the dividing line between problematic romance and severe love addiction
articles.summary: New research indicates that people with clinical love addiction experience much more severe relationship anxiety than those simply at risk. However, both groups share similar struggles with regulating their emotions.
